newsitem.title: USA: For male guppies, drab is a drag.
newsitem.headline: For male guppies, drab is a drag.

text.p: For guppies, beauty may be more than fin-deep.
Scientists have established that female guppies prefer bright, colourful guppy mates to drab males.
At first glance, this might seem rather stupid. The flashy bright males are a much easier target for hungry predators.
But according to Jean-Guy Godin, a researcher at Mount Allison University in Sackville, New Brunswick, the brighter males may have "superior overall quality" and better survival skills.
A female who mates with one therefore may have offspring with a better chance of outsmarting whatever larger animal is trying to turn him into lunch.
In research appearing in Tuesday's proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences, Godin reports on experiments where females picked the male who acted bolder when confronted with a predator.
When the predator was removed from the experiment, the females exhibited a clear preference for the brightly coloured males.

And, in bad news for their drab buddies who might dream of making up for their dull looks with wit, charm or attentiveness, Godin found, "Female mate choice was apparently not influenced by male courtship."
